extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and KIPO examiners (Republic of Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules under the Korean Patent Act and Enforcement Decree governing (A) prohibition/permission to file patent applications overseas for national-defense-related inventions and (B) eligibility, request, documentation, and evidentiary requirements for expedited examination (including utility models and special-case categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications banned from filing overseas
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Article 41 of the Patent Act, an invention crucial for national defense can be banned from filing overseas; if filed abroad without permission, the applicant is deemed to have abandoned the right to a patent and must pay reasonable compensation for losses due to violation of the ban.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications banned from filing overseas include those classified by a KIPO examiner as confidential or indicated by the applicant as national defense-related, and those deemed necessary to be kept confidential after consultation with the Defense Acquisition Program Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to file a banned application overseas (scope and conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Korean government grants permission to file a patent application banned from filing overseas, the application may exceptionally be filed in foreign countries — currently restricted by agreement to filing in the United States of America only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions for issuing permission include: (1) the specification's content must be clear and specific to enable examination in the U.S.; (2) the right to claim damages caused by confidentiality in the U.S. must be waived (except for damages from unauthorized U.S. use/disclosure). To obtain permission, submit a written request (Annexed Form No.21) and follow consultation procedures with the Defense Acquisition Program Administration. Detailed administrative instructions and implementation procedures govern the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and security requirements when filing in the U.S. with permission
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who files in the U.S. after receiving permission must attach and submit specified copies and security documents to Korean authorities and designate a U.S.-cleared representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: two copies of application documents, a copy of the KIPO-issued permission, a copy of the representative's personal information and U.S. security clearance; submit these to the Commissioner of the Defense Acquisition Program Administration. The representative must have U.S. government security clearance and initiate patent proceedings. The applicant must immediately notify the Commissioner of the Defense Acquisition Program Administration of the U.S. application number and date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of U.S.-filed national defense-related applications in Korea
rubrics_metrics.description: A national defense-related application kept confidential in the U.S. may be filed in the Republic of Korea subject to special filing materials and confidentiality handling by KIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing in Korea requires two copies of application documents, three copies of specification/abstract/drawings (one spec copy may omit the description), a copy of U.S. permission for filing in Korea, and relevant security-related documents. KIPO will keep the application confidential; detailed handling is in the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination general authority (Article 61)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may instruct an examiner to examine a patent application with priority to other applications where specified conditions exist (e.g., third-party commercial/industrial practice after laying-open or when urgently necessary by Presidential Decree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory authority is implemented via the Enforcement Decree and Directive listing categories of applications eligible for expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: defense-industry-related applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application directed to the art of the defense industry is an object eligible for expedited examination under Article 9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included explicitly in the enumerated list of eligible applications for expedited processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: green technology
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application directly related to green technology (defined broadly to include technologies minimizing greenhouse gas/pollutant emissions, energy/resource efficiency, clean energy, recycling, eco-friendliness, and related convergence technologies) is eligible for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Green-technology applications financially supported or certified under the Framework Act on Low Carbon Green Growth or other national policies can be entitled to expedited or super-expedited examination if notified search results are provided by a special institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: export promotion and official duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications directly related to export promotion, and applications relating to the official duties of the State or local governments (including certain national/public school duties), are eligible for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes patent applications concerning duties of national/public schools filed by technology transfer/commercialization offices within those schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: venture businesses and SMEs (various enterprise qualifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed by an enterprise confirmed as a venture business, by enterprises selected as technology-innovative SMEs, or by enterprises selected as exemplary in employee invention compensation systems are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility depends on meeting the enterprise qualification in the reference time window (see Reference Time). Specific statutory articles (Act on Special Measures for Promotion of Venture Businesses, Act on Promotion of Technology Innovation of SMEs, Invention Promotion Act) govern qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: results of state-supported projects / quality certification
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application relating to the results of state projects supporting new-technology development or quality certification is eligible for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to accelerate commercialization/public benefit from state-supported R&D outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: treaty-priority-basis pending abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application which serves as a basis of a priority claim under treaties (limited to where a foreign application claiming priority is pending before a foreign patent office) is eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is limited to cases where the foreign office has a pending application claiming priority to the Korean application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: invention being practiced or prepared by applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application whose invention is being practiced or is being prepared to be practiced by the patent applicant is eligible for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For foreigners, 'practicing' means practicing within the Republic of Korea; practicing outside Korea by a foreign applicant does not qualify. Practicing can also be by licensee or authorized person. If an independent claim meeting this condition exists, the whole application may be accepted for expedited examination (see Claims requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: electronic transaction relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application directly related to electronic transaction is eligible for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated in Article 9 as a specific eligible technical subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: bilateral/foreign-office agreements and authorized prior-art searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for which the Commissioner has agreed with a foreign patent office to expedite examination, or for which an authorized prior-art search institute was requested and will notify KIPO of results, are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where prior art searches are performed by designated specialized institutes, the requester may omit detailed prior-art explanation in the expedited request since search results serve as evidence of patentability/necessity of urgent processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: applicants aged over 65 or seriously ill
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application filed by a person over 65 or by a person unlikely to be able to perform proceedings due to serious health conditions (unless they can obtain expedited examination otherwise) can be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Enforcement Decree includes this humanitarian category; the requester must demonstrate the condition as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-case eligibility: high-tech medical complex R&D
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding Article 61, the Commissioner may direct priority examination for patent applications related to medical R&D within the High-Tech Medical Complex submitted by tenant medical R&D institutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is provided under the Special Act on the Designation and Support of High-Tech Medical Complex (Article 26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request expedited examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone, including the applicant, can request expedited examination; central or local governments (including technology transfer/commercialization offices of national/public schools) alone can request expedited examination for applications relating to governmental duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester is legally incompetent (minor, under guardianship), the legal representative must act. Unincorporated associations may request through their representative. Foreign-filed applications may be requested and are judged by the same criteria as Korean-filed applications, with special rules about the geographic meaning of 'practicing'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application types and filing-time eligibility for expedited examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications and utility-model registration applications filed after October 1, 2006 are eligible; dual applications (converted from utility model filed before Oct 1, 2006) can be entitled; request for substantive examination must be made before or at the same time as the request for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expedited system was introduced with the 2006 amendment that changed utility-model registration to substantive examination-based registration. Only applications falling within statutory date ranges are eligible as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference time for determining eligibility (timing rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility is assessed based on the status either at the time of the request for expedited examination or at the time of determining whether to accept it; changes in status between those times (e.g., becoming a venture company) can render an application eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: an applicant who becomes a venture company between request and determination may qualify; an application filed before a statutory change may be eligible if the expedited request was made after the change. If a third party was practicing at request time but stopped before determination (or vice versa), the application can still be recognized eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims requirement for eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention that makes the application eligible for expedited examination must be recited in the claims; inventions described only in the specification but not claimed are not recognized for expedited examination. Eligibility is determined based on claims as amended before the determination time. If any one claim is recognized eligible, the whole application may be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims providing eligibility are canceled by amendment before determination, the request will not be recognized. When assessing eligibility, examiners do not determine whether new matter is introduced, nor assess unity of invention or inventive step — only whether the claimed invention falls within eligible categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication (laying-open) requirement for third-party-practicing basis
rubrics_metrics.description: For requests based on a person other than the applicant practicing the invention, the application must be laid open; otherwise, laying-open/publication is not generally required for other bases of expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is about to be laid open (e.g., within 15 days), determination of eligibility may be deferred (not dismissed) until laying-open; if the applicant requested early disclosure, similar deferral rules apply. Once laid open, the examiner proceeds with expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity-of-urgent-processing standard and factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications eligible by category are, in principle, deemed necessary for urgent processing (except those based on third-party practicing); to determine necessity, the determining officer considers: (i) relevance to national policies, (ii) protection of the applicant's interest, and (iii) whether urgent processing would make grant of a patent likely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For factor (iii), submitting prior-art search results and an explanation of patentability supports the claim of necessity. Where prior-art searches are done by specialized institutes or under foreign-office agreements, the requester may omit detailed prior-art explanations because the institute's search suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art search disclosure and comparative explanation requirements for showing necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester must describe the search process and provide a comparative (contrastive) explanation between the claimed invention and the closest prior-art(s) to demonstrate why urgent processing is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles: disclose more than four closest prior arts where possible (fewer acceptable in new technical fields); describe similarities, differences, and contrastive analysis consecutively for each claim, with contrastive explanations for all independent claims (dependent claims may be omitted). If an independent claim lacks a contrastive explanation but is substantially the same as another explained independent claim, it may be deemed appropriately described. Additional search results (e.g., from local IP centers) may be submitted instead of search process details, but a contrastive explanation is still required in the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling where self-search results or contrastive explanation are missing or inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: If self-search results and contrastive explanation are not submitted or are inappropriately disclosed, the examiner will order supplementation; failure to comply or persistent insufficiency leads to rejection of the expedited-examination request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inappropriate disclosure includes omission of mandatory contents: (i) search processes and search results (more than four results) and independent claims, or (ii) contrastive explanation. However, finding additional prior art by the examiner that negates novelty/inventive step does not by itself mean the self-search was inappropriate. The self-search suffices if the examiner can easily comprehend results and explanation; applicants need not follow the exact Annexed Form No.5 if comprehension is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency and flexibility standard for self-search disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-search results and contrastive explanation are sufficient if an examiner can easily comprehend them; applicants need not strictly adhere to the Annexed Form No.5 disclosure format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special cases (e.g., new technical fields with few prior arts) can be recognized as adequate disclosures. Where prior art searches have been carried out by authorized institutes, the requester may omit detailed prior-art descriptions because those searches/explanations are treated as evidence of patentability/necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference on processing time when notifications cannot be sent
rubrics_metrics.description: When certain documents (change of applicant, change/resignation of representative, etc.) are received but an examiner cannot send a notification in response, processing time calculations exclude the period from receipt to acceptance of those documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if decision for expedited examination is on Feb 1, a change-of-applicant report submitted on Mar 20 and accepted after amendment Apr 20 would be treated so that processing time excludes the receipt-to-acceptance interval. (Guides calculation of statutory/target processing times.)
